item.name: ⭐ QA Demo (10 Endpoints)
item.description:
Run these in order 1→10 for the graded Postman demo.

⚠️ CRITICAL: After Step 4, copy the returned _id into the {{bookId}} collection variable before running Steps 6–10.

request.description:
ENDPOINT 1 of 10
Verifies the Express backend is running on port 5000.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { status: 'ok' }

ENDPOINT 2 of 10
Seeds a full demo textbook with pre-built content segments into MongoDB in one click.

✨ AUTO-CAPTURE SCRIPT INCLUDED:
Postman will automatically capture 'bookId' and 'bookSlug' into collection variables when this request is sent!

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK or 201 Created
  Body: { success: true, book: { _id, slug, title, ... } }

query.description: Clerk user ID whose books to retrieve

request.description:
ENDPOINT 3 of 10
Retrieves all books for the user. Confirm the demo book from Step 2 appears here. Also shows the slug you'll use in Step 4.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: [ { _id, title, author, slug, ... } ] }

ENDPOINT 4 of 10
Fetches a complete book document by its URL slug. This is exactly what the frontend reader calls when you open /books/[slug] — it loads full book metadata for the reading workspace.

✨ AUTO-RESOLVED:
Uses {{bookSlug}} variable auto-populated by Step 02!

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: { _id, title, author, slug, pdfURL, coverURL, ... } }

ENDPOINT 5 of 10
Returns all registered users with their total book count. Used by the admin dashboard to monitor platform usage.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: [ { _id, clerkId, email, role, bookCount, ... } ] }

ENDPOINT 6 of 10
Sends a user question to Groq LLM. The backend retrieves relevant book segments (RAG), builds context, then returns a structured markdown response as an academic tutor.

Also persists both the user message and AI reply into MongoDB (ChatMessage) — powering Step 9.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: '**Round Robin** is a...' }

ENDPOINT 7 of 10
Generates a structured study summary from real book segments via Groq LLM.

Returns markdown with 3 sections:
  📌 Executive Summary
  🔑 Key Takeaways
  📖 Important Terminology

Built by: John Vencie R. Sales
Commit: 'feat: add Groq chapter summary endpoint'

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: '### 📌 Executive Summary\n...' }

ENDPOINT 8 of 10
Generates a 5-question multiple choice quiz from real book content via Groq LLM.

Response Schema:
{
  quizTitle: string,
  questions: [{
    id: 1-5,
    question: string,
    options: [A, B, C, D],
    correctIndex: 0-3,
    explanation: string
  }]
}

Built by: John Vencie R. Sales
Commit: '[AI-02] AI Flashcard & Multiple Choice Quiz Generator'

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: { quizTitle: '...', questions: [...5 items] } }

ENDPOINT 9 of 10
Fetches the last 50 chat messages persisted in MongoDB for this book+user. Sorted chronologically.

Run AFTER Step 6 to prove messages were saved and survive page reloads.

Built by: John Vencie R. Sales
Commit: 'feat(chat): persist textbook conversations across sessions'

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: [ { role: 'user', content: '...', createdAt: '...' }, ... ] }

ENDPOINT 10 of 10
Permanently deletes all chat messages for this book+user pair from MongoDB.

Tip for demo: Run Step 9 AFTER this to confirm the array is now empty — proving DELETE worked.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, deletedCount: 2 }

request.description:
Creates or upserts a user in MongoDB from Clerk auth data. Called automatically by the app on first login — sending it manually here simulates that webhook.

Expected:
  Status: 200 OK
  Body: { success: true, data: { _id, clerkId, email, role, ... } }

Toggles a user's role between 'user' and 'admin'. Requires the MongoDB _id of the user (get it from Get All Users).

Update {{userId}} variable with a real MongoDB _id before running.

Expected:
  200 OK — { success: true, data: { role: 'admin' } }

Toggles a user's banned status. A banned user loses access to AI features and book management.

Update {{userId}} variable with a real MongoDB _id before running.

Expected:
  200 OK — { success: true, data: { isBanned: true } }

Permanently removes a user from the MongoDB User collection.

⚠️ Use with caution — this is irreversible.

Expected:
  200 OK — { success: true, message: 'User deleted' }
